title: Recipe 11 — Managed Multitenant (one daemon, many tenants, no shared storage)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 11 is the SaaS shape: one deployment, many customers, and isolation you can prove rather than promise.”
beats.script: Recipe 11 is the SaaS shape: one deployment, many customers, and isolation you can prove rather than promise. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens 11 managed multitenant.md now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to actually answer a run.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to actually answer a run. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, add the shared agent
beats.cue: “target: managed — a long-running gateway daemon. And one agent block, shared by every tenant.”
beats.script: Target: managed — a long-running gateway daemon. And one agent block, shared by every tenant. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 88 through 93 of 11 managed multitenant.md, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Declare tenant-a and its budget
beats.cue: “A tenant is an id plus a token budget — and the budget is a first-class spec field, not external policy.”
beats.script: A tenant is an id plus a token budget — and the budget is a first-class spec field, not external policy. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 94 through 98 of 11 managed multitenant.md become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Declare tenant-b
beats.cue: “Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree, its own audit chain.”
beats.script: Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree, its own audit chain. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 99 through 102 of 11 managed multitenant.md become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Only this next block is appended, so the specification grows in the same order the runtime will parse it.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”
beats.script: Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written. The gateway reads this, not the YAML.”
beats.script: The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written. The gateway reads this, not the YAML. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints the IR for target managed, tenants included.

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed, tenants included

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key. A gateway that can't answer is still a gateway that came up.”
beats.script: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key. A gateway that can't answer is still a gateway that came up. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window).

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window)

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — 351 lines of TypeScript you own outright.”
beats.script: JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — 351 lines of TypeScript you own outright. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash daemon.ts now. The relevant implementation is now visible, so the claim can be inspected directly instead of taken on faith.

beats.label: Hand it a weak signing secret
beats.cue: “Under sixteen characters and it refuses to start rather than serving tenants on a guessable secret. Exit 1, on purpose.”
beats.script: Under sixteen characters and it refuses to start rather than serving tenants on a guessable secret. Exit 1, on purpose. [[pause:1.5s]] The nonzero result is intentional: this command expects exit code 1. Deliberate rejection daemon.ts line 23 checks the length before it binds: “CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET is set but too short (min 16 chars). Refusing to start.” then process.exit(1).

verify.note: deliberate rejection — daemon.ts line 23 checks the length before it binds: “CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET is set but too short (min 16 chars). Refusing to start.” then process.exit(1). Set inline so it does not leak into the beats after it

beats.label: Pin the JWT secret
beats.cue: “Now a real one — at least sixteen chars — pinned so tokens survive a restart.”
beats.script: Now a real one — at least sixteen chars — pinned so tokens survive a restart. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it on stderr.

verify.note: without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it on stderr

beats.label: Put tenant storage under live/
beats.cue: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 20 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera instead of in /tmp.
beats.script: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 20 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera instead of in /tmp. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. Default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained.

verify.note: default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained

beats.label: Boot the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it.
beats.script: “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. The daemon binds with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials.

verify.note: the daemon binds with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-a
beats.cue: “JWT issuance is out of scope for the gateway — it only verifies.” Here that's local HS256 over the secret we just pinned.
beats.script: “JWT issuance is out of scope for the gateway — it only verifies.” Here that's local HS256 over the secret we just pinned. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; also proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle.
beats.command: TENANT_A_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-a" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; also proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-a
beats.cue: [needs-key] “JWT in, JSON-RPC out, audit log written.” One authenticated call and runs.create comes back with a runId.
beats.script: “JWT in, JSON-RPC out, audit log written.” One authenticated call and runs.create comes back with a runId. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. The crewhaus.v1 envelope, not the bare jsonrpc-2.0 one the recipe prints. sessionId is passed explicitly because the managed codegen's default id is rejected by session-store (it wants sess_<16 hex>).
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_A_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"1","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of France?","sessionId":"sess_0123456789abcdef"}}'

verify.note: the crewhaus.v1 envelope, not the bare jsonrpc-2.0 one the recipe prints. sessionId is passed explicitly because the managed codegen's default id is rejected by session-store (it wants sess_<16 hex>). Keyless it answers internal_error: no Anthropic credentials

groups.title: One more thing · the invariant target: managed exists to enforce

beats.label: Read tenant-a's audit chain
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Every event carries the SHA-256 of the prior event.” GENESIS, then hash, then hash — tampering is detectable, which is the property an auditor cares about.
beats.script: “Every event carries the SHA-256 of the prior event.” GENESIS, then hash, then hash — tampering is detectable, which is the property an auditor cares about. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Written by run-create: gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash.

verify.note: written by run-create: gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-b
beats.cue: Same daemon, same secret, a different tenant_id claim — and again no key involved.
beats.script: Same daemon, same secret, a different tenant_id claim — and again no key involved. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Keyless, like run-mint; tenant-b is the second id declared in the spec's tenants: block.
beats.command: TENANT_B_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-b" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless, like run-mint; tenant-b is the second id declared in the spec's tenants: block

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-b
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same endpoint, second tenant — the gateway rebases every storage path on the claim it just verified.
beats.script: Same endpoint, second tenant — the gateway rebases every storage path on the claim it just verified. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on the first authenticated call; same sessionId caveat as run-create.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_B_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"2","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of Japan?","sessionId":"sess_fedcba9876543210"}}'

verify.note: creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on the first authenticated call; same sessionId caveat as run-create

beats.label: Show the two tenant trees
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.” Two roots, no shared directory — that's the whole claim, on disk.
beats.script: “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.” Two roots, no shared directory — that's the whole claim, on disk. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. After both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree.

verify.note: after both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree

beats.label: Stop the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon before it holds :3000 forever.
beats.script: Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon before it holds :3000 forever. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. Job %1 is the daemon run-boot backgrounded into this same terminal.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon run-boot backgrounded into this same terminal
